correctness.rationale: The standard 27 Picard line classes consist of 6 E_i, 15 F_ij and 6 G_i; their intersection pairing is diag(1,-1^6). Applying the published deck matrix produces nine 3-cycles. Independently enumerating all 2925 triples of 27 lines gives exactly 45 pairwise-intersecting line triples and 135 intersecting pairs. Their projections give precisely 9 singleton tritangents and 12 triple-blocks, each appearing 3 times; the 12 blocks cover all 36 pairs of nine orbit labels exactly once. The affine translation/SL_2(F3) quotient acts transitively on flexes and Hesse lines; deck C3 permutes the three lifts over each affine line, proving group orbits 9+36 and orders 648/9=72,648/36=18. The exact finite enumeration is exhaustive for these 27 classes; identification of the deck and family monodromy is imported from Medrano primary source.

originality.rationale: Medrano identifies nine flex-based triples and proves order-648 monodromy but does not state the full tritangent-projection Steiner triple system or induced 9+36 orbit classification. Brundu–Logar–Polli enumerate 45 tritangents and describe Hesse nine-Eckardt special cubic geometry, but their inspected sections do not give deck-orbit projection on smooth cyclic cubic family. A classical trihedral description may encode the same structure.
residual_risks: The identification of triple deck orbits with flex points and full monodromy relies on Medrano; independently checked line incidence does not prove those geometric premises.
An older classical cubic-surface trihedral-pair theorem might implicitly determine the same 9+36 Hesse Steiner system.
Projective automorphism orbits of an individual special cubic are not claimed.

value.rationale: The complete incidence of tritangent planes with the cyclic covering is a natural classical cubic-surface invariant and gives a nontrivial identification with the Hesse affine plane plus exact monodromy orbit decomposition, not just the known count 45.
